question: Explain why the power factor of an AC circuit becomes unity when voltage and current are in the same phase.

options.A: When voltage and current are in phase, $\phi=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and the power factor is zero.
options.B: The power factor is unity because the average power is always zero for in-phase voltage and current.
options.C: When voltage and current are in phase, $\phi=0$, so power factor $\cos\phi=1$. Hence $P=VI\cos\phi=VI$, giving maximum real power for the given rms voltage and current.
options.D: The power factor becomes unity because the voltage and current are $180^\circ$ out of phase.
